answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy rests on per-operator stake bonding tied to attested hardware keys. Each agent locks a bond in escrow, and the registry maps every wallet to one operator identity. When clustering finds two identities sharing an operator key, both bonds are burned, not just the newer. Cost to an attacker scales linearly: a thousand fake votes needs a thousand bonds, all forfeited on first detection. So one honest seat is cheaper than a canyon of ghosts, and fake quorum sits beyond the horizon of any budget. Attested logs let a quill of signed evidence trigger review.
